docs.title: NeuralNACA
docs.text:
A physics-embedded neural surrogate for NACA 4-digit airfoil polars that matches XFOIL more closely than NeuralFoil, trained on 0.052 % of NeuralFoil's XFOIL runs.

import neuralnaca
aero = neuralnaca.get_aero("NACA 2412", alpha=4.0, Re=1e6)

NeuralNACA predicts lift, drag and pitching moment as XFOIL 6.99 computes them (free transition, Ncrit = 9, Mach 0) for NACA 4-digit sections with 0-8 % camber and 6-18 % thickness, at Reynolds numbers from 105 to 107 and -5° to 15° incidence.

  • Physics where it is known. A differentiable panel method gives the inviscid lift and moment; the architecture is exactly mirror-symmetric; a flat-plate prior anchors the drag. A small ensemble learns only the viscous correction. → Method
  • A careful comparison. Five independent replications, all eight NeuralFoil sizes, paired bootstrap intervals, five definitions of the XFOIL ground truth, ablations and a data-efficiency curve. → Benchmark protocol, Results
  • Honest about failure. Where XFOIL itself fails, predictions are flagged; where the model is weak, it says so. → Limitations
  • Reproducible by construction. Data, models and results ship with checksums; every number in these pages is generated and tested; neuralnaca reproduce re-derives them at three depths. → Reproducing the results

docs.title: The result in one table
docs.text:
5 independent replications (each with its own Sobol training set of 4,096 XFOIL runs = 0.052 % of NeuralFoil's 7,913,292, and its own i.i.d. test set of unseen airfoils); 13,933 XFOIL-converged test points in total. Ratios are NeuralNACA / NeuralFoil-xxxlarge with 95 % paired-bootstrap intervals (< 1: NeuralNACA more accurate).

output NeuralNACA MAE NeuralFoil MAE MAE ratio RMSE ratio NeuralNACA median NeuralFoil median CL 0.0031 0.0050 0.62 [0.58, 0.65] 0.97 [0.82, 1.15] 0.00080 0.00236 ln CD 0.0092 0.0142 0.65 [0.62, 0.68] 0.88 [0.80, 0.97] 0.00306 0.00717 CM 0.00052 0.00086 0.60 [0.57, 0.64] 0.99 [0.82, 1.21] 0.000152 0.000444

NeuralNACA is a specialist (one airfoil family, one flow model, a bounded domain) compared with a generalist. Its advantage comes mainly from modelling the exact NACA geometry, which NeuralFoil approximates with a Kulfan fit to which XFOIL is surprisingly sensitive (see Results). It is not a general replacement for NeuralFoil, and all errors are relative to XFOIL, not to experiments.

docs.title: Benchmark protocol
docs.text:
Question. For NACA 4-digit sections inside the domain, is NeuralNACA, trained on a few thousand XFOIL runs, more accurate with respect to XFOIL than NeuralFoil, which was trained on 7.9 million XFOIL runs?

Everything below is implemented in neuralnaca.benchmark and executed by neuralnaca bench .... The shipped files in data/ and benchmarks/ are its outputs, and Reproducing the results re-derives them.

docs.title: Ground truth
docs.text:
setting value why solver XFOIL 6.99 (python module, commit 5c8c4ff, built without floating-point traps) the program NeuralFoil was trained to imitate geometry exact NACA 4-digit coordinates (100 per side, cosine spacing) what a user would hand to either tool panels 279 (XFOIL PPAR re-panelling) AeroSandbox's default, used for NeuralFoil's data transition free, \(N_\mathrm{crit} = 9\) NeuralFoil's default Mach 0 iterations 100 AeroSandbox's default protocol cold start for every point answers independent of run order (see below) scoring XFOIL-converged points only there is no reference value otherwise

The executable backend reproduces the module's results to the four printed decimals at benign conditions. At conditions where XFOIL has more than one solution, the two backends (like any two protocols) can land on different branches; this is part of the noise floor quantified below.

docs.title: Data and replications
docs.text:
Each replication \(s\) (seeds 0-4) consists of:

  • a training set: 4,096 conditions from a scrambled Sobol design (seed \(s\)), 20 % of them forced to be symmetric sections, Re log-uniform, angles rounded to 0.001°;
  • a test set: 3,000 conditions drawn i.i.d. uniformly (independent generator, seed \(s + 1000\)), so that the test error is an unbiased estimate of the domain-averaged error;
  • a model trained on the converged training points with the fixed recipe;
  • an evaluation on the converged test points.

No test airfoil occurs in any form in the training set of its replication (checked in every run, and the run aborts otherwise). The sections in the documentation figures (0012, 2412, 4412, 6409) occur in no training set at all. The test suite verifies both properties on the shipped files.

Replications 0-2 were generated during development, but their test sets were never used to choose anything. Replications 3 and 4 were generated and evaluated after the code freeze. Five replications give an honest picture of the run-to-run spread caused by the random data draw and the training randomness together; a separate study isolates the training randomness.

docs.title: NeuralFoil configuration
docs.text:
• neuralfoil.get_aero_from_coordinates(coordinates, alpha, Re, n_crit=9, model_size=...) with free transition (xtr_upper = xtr_lower = 1).
  • The same exact NACA coordinates that XFOIL receives. NeuralFoil fits its 8+8-weight Kulfan parameterisation to them internally; that fitting step is part of NeuralFoil's pipeline and therefore of its error. The truth-sensitivity study separates the two.
  • All eight model sizes (xxsmall ... xxxlarge); xxxlarge, the largest, is the primary reference.
  • Version 0.3.3 (recorded in every result file).

docs.title: Metrics and statistics
docs.text:
• The primary metrics are NeuralFoil's own: mean absolute error (MAE) of \(C_L\), \(\ln C_D\) and \(C_M\). An error of 0.01 in \(\ln C_D\) is about 1 % of drag.
  • Secondary metrics: RMSE (sensitive to the largest errors), median absolute error (typical case), 95th percentile, mean relative drag error, the share of points where one model is closer to XFOIL, and a breakdown by angle of attack and Reynolds number.
  • Uncertainty: the ratio of MAEs (NeuralNACA / NeuralFoil) with a 95 % paired bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of test points; both models are always scored on the same points). A distribution-free Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the paired absolute errors complements it. The bootstrap's coverage is itself tested in the test suite.
  • Claim criterion: NeuralNACA "beats" NeuralFoil on an output if the upper end of the 95 % interval of the MAE ratio is below 1. The central claim requires this for all three outputs, in every replication and pooled.

docs.title: Training-data accounting
docs.text:
• NeuralNACA: 4,096 XFOIL runs attempted per model (about 93 % converged).
  • NeuralFoil: 7,913,292 XFOIL runs attempted, 56 % converged (Sharpe & Hansman, arXiv:2503.16323, Sec. III.E).

Both counts include non-converged runs. The ratio, 0.052 %, compares the XFOIL effort of the two approaches. It does not compare their scope: NeuralFoil is a generalist (arbitrary airfoils, ±180° incidence, Re from 10² to 10¹⁰, variable transition settings), NeuralNACA a specialist for one airfoil family in a bounded domain.

docs.title: Threats to validity, and how each is addressed
docs.text: concern how it is addressed A specialist is compared with a generalist Stated up front everywhere; the domain and the family are fixed in advance; the claim is restricted to them. The ground-truth protocol and geometry differ from those NeuralFoil was trained on Truth-sensitivity study: both models scored against five XFOIL definitions, including NeuralFoil's own protocol on NeuralFoil's own geometry, with a control that separates the frame transformation from the shape fit. Hyper-parameters tuned on the test data Tuned on separate development draws; replications 3-4 generated after the freeze. One lucky data draw Five independent replications plus a pooled analysis; per-replication results are all reported. Training randomness Training-seed study on fixed data; its spread sets the reproduction tolerance. Averages hide failures Medians, 95th percentiles, RMSE, error distributions, regime breakdowns, and an explicit search for worst cases (see Limitations). Only converged points are scored The share and location of non-converged points are reported; NeuralNACA flags them as unsupported, and the accuracy on supported points is reported separately. XFOIL is not unique near stall XFOIL-vs-XFOIL differences between protocols bound the attainable accuracy and are reported next to the model errors. Leakage between training and test Airfoil-level disjointness checked in every run and in the test suite. Software versions Every result file records Python, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch, NeuralFoil, AeroSandbox and the XFOIL build. Silent drift between data, models, results and documentation SHA-256 manifest; every number in the documentation is generated from the result files, and tests fail if they disagree.

docs.title: Sensitivity to the ground truth
docs.text:
The test points of replication 0 are re-solved under five definitions of "what XFOIL says":

name protocol geometry iterations cold/naca cold start per point exact NACA (the benchmark's ground truth) 100 cold/naca-normalized cold start per point exact NACA, in NeuralFoil's normalised frame (control) 100 cold/kulfan cold start per point NeuralFoil's 8+8 Kulfan fit, in its normalised frame 100 nf-sweep/naca NeuralFoil's warm-started 5° sweeps from 0° exact NACA 200 nf-sweep/kulfan NeuralFoil's warm-started 5° sweeps from 0° NeuralFoil's Kulfan fit 200
  • nf-sweep/kulfan is how NeuralFoil's training labels were produced (see asb.XFoil.alpha(start_at=0) and NeuralFoil's training/ scripts), so it is the definition most favourable to NeuralFoil.
  • Comparing cold/naca with cold/naca-normalized isolates NeuralFoil's frame transformation (rotation and scaling to its normalised frame, angle and Reynolds-number adjustment, moment transfer).
  • Comparing cold/naca-normalized with cold/kulfan isolates the effect of the Kulfan shape fit.

Both models are scored on the points that converged under all definitions, and the study reports how much XFOIL disagrees with itself between definitions. Results: Results.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses semantic versioning. Changes that alter model predictions bump the weights' feature version and are always called out.
First public release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• neuralnaca package: prediction API (get_aero, NeuralNACA), shipped 5-member ensemble trained on 4,096 XFOIL runs (fingerprint 5988ce08779e0f31), training-support flag and ensemble spread with every prediction.
  • Differentiable Hess-Smith panel method, exactly mirror-symmetric architecture, flat-plate drag prior.
  • Robust XFOIL batch driver (python-module and executable backends, crash containment, cold-start and NeuralFoil-sweep protocols, Kulfan geometry), self-describing data sets with provenance.
  • Benchmark pipeline (neuralnaca bench): five replications against all NeuralFoil sizes, training-seed variance, ablations (including a physics-only baseline and autograd PINN residuals), data-efficiency curve (512-8,192 runs), ground-truth sensitivity (cold vs. NeuralFoil's sweep protocol; exact vs. Kulfan geometry, with a frame-only control), support and ensemble-spread study, speed comparison; generated tables and figures.
  • neuralnaca reproduce with three verification levels; SHA-256 manifest of all shipped files.
  • Scripts that rebuild the benchmark's XFOIL builds (verified to reproduce the shipped data bit for bit), and neuralnaca xfoil-check, which detects broken builds such as the Debian/Ubuntu package.
  • Documentation site and test suite (unit, property-based, physics validation, end-to-end, integrity of shipped results and documentation numbers).

docs.title: Fixed (relative to the pre-release script)
docs.text:
• The camber-position gate was an odd function of camber (tanh(m/0.01)), which broke the claimed exact reflection symmetry for negative camber. It is now even (1 - exp(-(m/0.01)^2)) and checked on every run (feature version 2; version-1 weights are refused).
  • OneCycleLR failed for training runs shorter than ~40 steps.
  • NumPy arrays in model metadata could not be serialised.
  • XFOIL worker processes that could not start (no __main__ guard) silently produced all-NaN data; this is now an explicit error.

docs.title: Rules for changes
docs.text:
• Anything that changes predictions (features, architecture, panel discretisation, training recipe) must bump FEATURES_VERSION in neuralnaca/model.py if old weights become incompatible, retrain the shipped model, re-run the benchmark (neuralnaca bench ..., see docs/reference/cli.md), regenerate tables and figures (neuralnaca report && neuralnaca figures), update benchmarks/MANIFEST.json (python scripts/make_manifest.py) and the README headline, and be described in CHANGELOG.md. The integrity tests enforce consistency.
  • Numbers in the documentation are never typed by hand: they come from docs/results/tables.md, which is generated.
  • Keep negative results. If an idea does not help, document it rather than dropping it silently.
  • New behaviour needs tests; bug fixes need a regression test.

docs.title: Reporting a discrepancy with the published results
docs.text: Please run neuralnaca reproduce --level 0 --json report.json and neuralnaca info, and attach both files to the issue.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
How can a model trained on 0.05 % of NeuralFoil's data be more accurate? Mostly because of geometry, and partly because of specialisation, and not because it is a better XFOIL emulator.

  • Geometry. NeuralFoil does not see the NACA section itself: it analyses an 8+8-weight Kulfan (CST) fit of it. The fit is geometrically excellent (shape errors of hundredths of a percent of chord), but XFOIL's transition prediction is sensitive enough that the fitted shape gives a noticeably different answer. That difference is about as large as NeuralFoil's entire error against the exact section. Scored against XFOIL on its own fitted shape, NeuralFoil is more accurate than NeuralNACA. Even a plain MLP without physics, trained on 4,096 exact-geometry XFOIL runs, beats NeuralFoil on NACA sections.
  • Specialisation. NeuralFoil must represent every airfoil shape, ±180° of incidence, Reynolds numbers from 10² to 10¹⁰ and arbitrary transition settings with one network. NeuralNACA covers one three-parameter family in a bounded box at one transition setting.
  • Physics. The panel-method backbone lowers the error by 17-29 % relative to the same model without it.

See the ground-truth study and the ablation. The comparison says nothing about which tool is better in general.

Is this a physics-informed neural network (PINN)? In the broad sense, yes: physics is built into the architecture (panel-method baseline and features, exact symmetry, drag prior). In the narrow sense of a PDE-residual loss, no. That option is implemented, but it does not help here (see Method and the ablation). Of the built-in ingredients only the panel method measurably improves accuracy; the symmetry and the drag prior make the model consistent rather than more accurate.

Is the comparison fair to NeuralFoil? We tried to make it as fair as we could, and to make every choice checkable.

  • Both models get the same exact coordinates and conditions and are scored on the same converged points.
  • The XFOIL settings match NeuralFoil's data pipeline: 279 panels, \(N_\mathrm{crit} = 9\), 100 iterations.
  • All eight NeuralFoil sizes are reported.
  • The comparison is repeated under five definitions of the XFOIL ground truth, including NeuralFoil's own warm-started protocol on its own Kulfan geometry.

The remaining asymmetry is intrinsic: we chose the family and the domain. See the threats-to-validity table.

Why a cold start for every XFOIL point? So that a label does not depend on which other points were solved, or in what order. This makes data sets order-independent, parallelisable and extensible (the Sobol prefixes of the data-efficiency curve rely on it). The cost is that near stall a cold start can land on a different solution branch than a warm-started sweep. The ground-truth study measures how much that matters.

Why 279 panels? It is AeroSandbox's default re-panelling, which NeuralFoil's training data used. Evaluating against XFOIL at 160 panels (XFOIL's default) would make NeuralFoil look about 10 % worse, which would be unfair to it.

Can I use it for NACA 5-digit / 6-series / my own airfoil? Not with the shipped model. The pipeline is generic in principle: replace the geometry, panel nodes and features, and retrain. The package does not do this for you. For arbitrary shapes, use NeuralFoil.

Can I get gradients for optimisation? Yes. Everything from the geometry parameters to the outputs is a PyTorch graph; see Predictions → Gradients. The shipped weights are smooth, but keep the support flag in mind: an optimiser will happily exploit unsupported regions.

How fast is it? See Cost per prediction. It is far faster than XFOIL. Compared with NeuralFoil it depends on the batch shape: NeuralNACA needs one small panel solve per distinct airfoil, so many angles or Reynolds numbers on the same section are very cheap.

The numbers I get differ in the last digits. On another platform, retraining changes the weights slightly; see Reproducing the results. Predictions from the shipped weights should agree to about 10⁻⁶. If they do not, please open an issue with the output of neuralnaca info and neuralnaca reproduce --level 0 --json report.json.

Why is CD sometimes enormous? You are almost certainly outside the training support (deep stall of a thin section at low Reynolds number, where XFOIL itself does not converge). Check supported; an UnsupportedWarning should have been raised. See Limitations.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
NeuralNACA needs Python ≥ 3.10. What else you install depends on what you want to do:

goal install needs XFOIL? predict polars with the shipped model pip install neuralnaca (or from the repository, below) no compare against NeuralFoil, regenerate figures pip install "neuralnaca[neuralfoil,plot]" no verify / retrain the published results (levels 0-1) repository checkout + pip install -e ".[neuralfoil,plot,test]" no generate new XFOIL data, reproduce level 2 the above + XFOIL (below) yes 
git clone https://github.com/KeepCoolWithCoolidge/NeuralNACA.git
cd NeuralNACA
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"      # everything: neuralfoil, matplotlib, test and docs tools
neuralnaca info                        # versions, shipped model fingerprint, XFOIL availability

The runtime dependencies are only NumPy, SciPy and PyTorch (CPU is enough; the model is small).

docs.title: XFOIL
docs.text: XFOIL is the "teacher" that produced every training and test label. It is not needed to make predictions or to verify the published numbers from the shipped data, only to generate new data. Two interchangeable backends are supported; you need one of them.

docs.title: Option A: the xfoil Python module (recommended, about 4x faster)
docs.text:
bash scripts/install_xfoil_python.sh
neuralnaca xfoil-check --backend module

The script clones xfoil-python at the exact commit used for the benchmark (5c8c4ff), removes its floating-point-trap compiler flags and installs it with pip. It needs git, cmake, gfortran and a C compiler (Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install git cmake gfortran build-essential; macOS: brew install cmake gcc).

Why patch the compiler flags?

Upstream compiles XFOIL with -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero -finit-real=inf -fbounds-check. With traps enabled, a floating-point exception inside the viscous solver kills the whole Python process instead of merely failing to converge. The benchmark data were generated without traps (-O2 -fdefault-real-8). We verified that a fresh build made with the script reproduces the shipped XFOIL results bit for bit.

docs.title: Option B: an XFOIL 6.99 executable
docs.text:
bash scripts/build_xfoil_binary.sh ~/opt/xfoil          # Debian/Ubuntu: builds from the distribution's source package
export NEURALNACA_XFOIL=~/opt/xfoil/xfoil
neuralnaca xfoil-check --backend binary

The executable is found through executable=..., then $NEURALNACA_XFOIL, then xfoil on the PATH. Every point runs in its own XFOIL process, which is slower but immune to crashes and hangs.

Distribution packages can be broken

The binary shipped by Debian/Ubuntu (apt install xfoil) aborts with a floating-point exception on most viscous points. neuralnaca xfoil-check detects this (it prints FAIL and NaNs). Rebuild it with the script above. On other systems, build the official sources after removing -ffpe-trap=..., -finit-real=inf and -fbounds-check from the Makefiles (and adding -fallow-argument-mismatch for gfortran ≥ 10). The script reproduces the benchmark's binary byte for byte on Ubuntu.

docs.title: Checking an XFOIL installation
docs.text: neuralnaca xfoil-check solves three reference conditions and compares them with the build used for the benchmark (tolerances 0.005 in CL, 0.0002 in CD, 0.003 in CM). The test suite goes further: pytest -m xfoil checks that your XFOIL reproduces 24 points of the shipped test set and exercises both solution protocols.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text: The package is pure Python plus PyTorch and runs wherever PyTorch runs (Linux, macOS, Windows). The published results were produced on Linux x86-64; see Reproducing the results for what "reproducible" means across platforms.

docs.text:

mkdocs serve          # or: mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: This page lists, as concretely as we can, where NeuralNACA should not be trusted, and what the benchmark does not show. Most items were found by deliberately looking for failures; several are covered by tests.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• One family, one box. NACA 4-digit sections with \(0 \le m \le 0.08\), \(0.2 \le p \le 0.7\), \(0.06 \le t \le 0.18\), \(10^5 \le \mathrm{Re} \le 10^7\), \(-5^\circ \le \alpha \le 15^\circ\). Nothing is claimed outside this box. NACA 5-digit, 6-series and arbitrary sections are not supported.
  • One flow model. Free transition with \(N_\mathrm{crit} = 9\), Mach 0, no forced trips, no flaps, two-dimensional. NeuralFoil covers all of these; NeuralNACA covers none of them.
  • A specialist against a generalist. NeuralFoil was trained for arbitrary airfoils across a much larger flow domain. Beating it on its home ground with a small fraction of the data is a statement about what a specialist can do in a narrow family, not about which tool is better in general.

docs.title: What the advantage is, and what it is not
docs.text:
NeuralNACA predicts XFOIL for the exact NACA section; NeuralFoil predicts XFOIL for its own 8+8-weight Kulfan fit of it. The ground-truth study shows that the two XFOIL answers differ by about as much as NeuralFoil's whole error. A control with the exact shape in NeuralFoil's coordinate frame shows that the frame transformation contributes almost nothing to \(C_L\) and \(C_D\), so the shape fit is the cause. Against XFOIL on its own fitted geometry, NeuralFoil is the more accurate model.

So the benchmark establishes that for NACA 4-digit sections, NeuralNACA is closer to XFOIL than NeuralFoil, mainly because it represents the geometry exactly and is specialised to it. It does not establish that NeuralNACA is a more faithful XFOIL emulator in general, or that physics embedding beats a large data set. A plain network trained on the same exact-geometry data also beats NeuralFoil here (see the ablation).

docs.title: The ground truth is XFOIL, not reality
docs.text: Every error reported here is an error with respect to XFOIL 6.99. XFOIL's own errors are inherited unchanged. They grow near and beyond maximum lift, at low Reynolds number with long laminar separation bubbles, and for thick sections at high incidence. Nothing in this project validates against wind-tunnel data.

docs.title: Where XFOIL does not converge, the model is unsupported, and can be absurd
docs.text:
About 7 % of random conditions in the domain do not converge in XFOIL. They concentrate in deep stall of thin sections at low Reynolds number. For example, none of the 27 points of the shipped model's training set with \(t < 0.08\), \(\mathrm{Re} < 2\times10^5\) and \(\alpha > 10^\circ\) converged. The model never saw data there, and its drag extrapolates without bound. NACA 0006 at Re = 10⁵ and 15° yields \(C_D \approx 6.6\), which is physically meaningless.

These conditions cannot be scored (XFOIL has no answer), so the benchmark is silent about them. Instead, NeuralNACA flags them. supported is false and an UnsupportedWarning is raised when the estimated XFOIL convergence probability is below 0.5 or the predicted drag exceeds the largest drag in the training data. How well this flag works on held-out data is reported in Results. It does not catch every non-converged condition, because XFOIL's failures are partly random. A test pins the behaviour for the known-bad corner.

docs.title: Sparse corners with sharp physics: rare but large errors
docs.text:
The advantage over NeuralFoil is an advantage on average and in the typical case. Among the worst individual errors of NeuralNACA, one pattern recurs. Highly cambered sections (\(m \approx 0.07\)-\(0.08\)) at low Reynolds number (1-2 × 10⁵) and negative incidence develop lower-surface separation. XFOIL converges there, but 4,096 training runs sample this corner sparsely. In one replication the five worst points account for more than half of NeuralNACA's squared \(C_L\) error (a third for NeuralFoil), and errors in \(C_L\) of up to 0.37 occur where NeuralFoil is within 0.01.

Consequence: RMSE, which is dominated by the largest errors, does not consistently favour NeuralNACA. In some replications the \(C_L\) or \(C_M\) RMSE ratio is above 1 (see the per-replication table in Results). If your application cares about worst-case rather than typical error in that corner, NeuralFoil is the more robust choice there, or NeuralNACA needs more training data in it.

Mitigation: the ensemble spread is a good indicator of these errors. It correlates with the actual error, and most of the largest errors have a spread in the top 5 % (statistics in Results). Check CL_std / CM_std.

docs.title: Low-Reynolds-number behaviour
docs.text: At \(\mathrm{Re} \approx 10^5\) XFOIL's polars are strongly non-linear even at small incidence. NACA 0012's lift jumps from 0 to 0.26 between 0° and 1° because of laminar separation. NeuralNACA reproduces this but slightly smooths it. Plausibility tests therefore apply the thin-airfoil lift-slope band only at \(\mathrm{Re} \ge 5\times10^5\).

docs.title: Uncertainty outputs are heuristic
docs.text: The ensemble standard deviations rank errors well but are not calibrated confidence intervals: five members are too few, and they share the same training data, so they can agree and still be wrong in the same direction.

docs.title: The panel method is a feature extractor, not a converged potential-flow solution
docs.text: With the open NACA trailing edge, the discrete Kutta condition makes the 120-panel solution drift slowly under refinement instead of converging (details in Method). At the fixed resolution used it is within 2 % of XFOIL's inviscid lift, and the network corrects the rest. Do not use neuralnaca.panel as a reference inviscid solver for open-trailing-edge sections without closing the gap.

docs.title: Dependence on how the ground truth is defined
docs.text: XFOIL's answer depends on the solution protocol (cold start vs. warm-started sweeps) and on the exact geometry (NACA coordinates vs. NeuralFoil's Kulfan fit), mostly near stall. NeuralNACA was trained on cold-start labels of the exact geometry, the setting it is scored on. The sensitivity study re-scores both models under five definitions, including NeuralFoil's own.

docs.title: Reproducibility across machines
docs.text: Results are bit-for-bit reproducible on the same platform and software versions (verified). On other CPUs, BLAS libraries or PyTorch versions, floating-point summation order can differ, and training amplifies such differences. Retrained models then differ slightly. The size of this effect is bounded by the training-seed study and is what the level-1 reproduction tolerance is based on. XFOIL builds other than the documented one can differ near stall; use neuralnaca xfoil-check.

docs.title: Things we tried that did not help
docs.text:
Kept here so that nobody has to rediscover them. All were evaluated on development draws separate from the benchmark.

  • Autograd PINN residuals (lift-slope band, curvature bound, drag monotonic in Re) on unlabelled collocation points: consistent with XFOIL but no accuracy gain, at several times the training cost (also measured in the ablation).
  • Boundary-layer integral features (Thwaites/Michel transition estimates, Squire-Young drag): hurt at this data size. The features are noisy near the separation boundaries where the error is concentrated.
  • Inviscid \(C_{p,\min}\) and other extra inviscid features: no gain.
  • Wider networks: no gain at 4,096 runs.
  • Mirror symmetry and the drag prior are kept for consistency and robustness, but in the ablation neither measurably improves the MAE (changes of at most 4 %). Earlier development runs with single networks suggested a small gain from the symmetry; the ensemble benchmark does not confirm it.
  • Training on fewer than about 2,000 runs: NeuralNACA falls behind NeuralFoil (see the data-efficiency curve).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
NeuralNACA approximates the map

\[ (m, p, t, \mathrm{Re}, \alpha) \;\longmapsto\; (C_L,\; \ln C_D,\; C_M) \]

that XFOIL 6.99 defines for NACA 4-digit sections (free transition, \(N_\mathrm{crit} = 9\), Mach 0). It is a physics-embedded neural network: classical aerodynamics supplies a baseline and the structure of the model, and an ensemble of small neural networks learns the viscous correction from XFOIL data.

Is this a PINN?

Not in the narrow sense of a network trained to satisfy a PDE residual. The physics enters through (1) a differentiable potential-flow panel solution used as baseline and as input features, (2) an exactly enforced reflection symmetry, and (3) a flat-plate skin-friction prior. An optional autograd-residual loss (the classic PINN ingredient) is implemented but off by default, because the ablation study finds it does not improve accuracy. The ablation quantifies what each ingredient contributes: the panel method improves accuracy markedly, while the symmetry and the drag prior mainly guarantee consistency.

docs.title: 1. Geometry
docs.text:
The NACA 4-digit section with maximum camber \(m\) at chordwise position \(p\) and thickness \(t\) has the half thickness

\[ y_t = 5t\,(0.2969\sqrt{x} - 0.1260x - 0.3516x^2 + 0.2843x^3 - 0.1015x^4) \]

(the classical open-trailing-edge form, as generated by XFOIL's NACA command) applied perpendicular to the camber line \(y_c = \tfrac{m}{p^2}(2px - x^2)\) for \(x < p\) and \(\tfrac{m}{(1-p)^2}((1-2p) + 2px - x^2)\) otherwise. neuralnaca.naca4_coordinates produces the coordinates given to XFOIL and NeuralFoil (100 points per side, cosine spacing); the panel method uses the same formula in PyTorch.

docs.title: 2. Inviscid baseline: a differentiable Hess-Smith panel method
docs.text:
The section is discretised into \(N = 120\) straight panels (cosine spacing). Each panel carries a constant source strength \(\sigma_j\), and all panels share one vortex strength \(\gamma\). Flow tangency at the \(N\) panel midpoints and the Kutta condition (equal tangential velocity on the two trailing-edge panels) give \(N+1\) linear equations.

Potential flow is linear in the free-stream vector, so the system is solved once for a unit free stream along \(x\) and once along \(y\). The lift then follows from the Kutta-Joukowski theorem (\(C_L = 2\Gamma/V_\infty c\)) and the quarter-chord moment from integrating \(C_p = 1 - V_t^2/V_\infty^2\). Both are closed-form functions of \(\alpha\):

\[ C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha) = A_L\cos\alpha + B_L\sin\alpha, \qquad C_{M,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha) = A_M - \left(B_M\cos^2\alpha + C_M\cos\alpha\sin\alpha + D_M\sin^2\alpha\right). \]

The six constants depend only on the geometry. They are computed once per airfoil (neuralnaca.panel.airfoil_constants, a batched dense solve), and the network evaluates the closed form, so \(\partial C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}/\partial\alpha\) is exact.

Validation (test suite, tests/test_panel.py).

  • On Joukowski airfoils the lift converges monotonically to the exact conformal-mapping solution under refinement. Convergence is slow, as expected for constant-source panels at a cusped trailing edge.
  • For closed-trailing-edge NACA sections, successive refinements change \(C_L\) by less than 0.1 %. At 960 panels the result agrees with XFOIL's inviscid lift for NACA 4412 to 0.2 % (XFOIL closes the trailing-edge gap with its own panel).
  • At the 120 panels used by the model, inviscid \(C_L\) is within 2 % (relative) and \(C_M\) within 0.0065 of XFOIL's own inviscid solution for seven sections and four angles.
  • Lift and moment satisfy the reflection identities to round-off. Lift from circulation agrees with lift from integrated pressure. The lift slope matches \(2\pi(1 + 0.77t)\) for NACA 0012, and the zero-lift angle of NACA 2412 matches thin-airfoil theory.

Known property: open trailing edge

The NACA definition leaves a small trailing-edge gap (0.25 % of \(t\)). With the Kutta condition applied across that gap, the discrete solution drifts slowly under refinement (about −0.7 % in \(C_L\) per doubling) instead of converging; XFOIL avoids this by closing the gap with a source panel. The model uses a fixed 120-panel discretisation, so the inviscid quantities are deterministic features within 2 % of XFOIL's inviscid answer, and the network learns the remaining difference. A test pins the size of the drift. A trailing-edge gap panel is a candidate improvement for a future feature version (it would require retraining).

docs.title: 3. Drag prior
docs.text:
\(\ln C_D\) is predicted as a correction to a flat-plate turbulent skin-friction estimate with a thickness form factor:

\[ C_{D,0} = 2\,C_f\,(1 + 2t + 60t^4), \qquad C_f = \frac{0.455}{(\log_{10}\mathrm{Re})^{2.58}} \quad \text{(Prandtl-Schlichting)}. \]

It captures the dominant Reynolds-number and thickness dependence of profile drag, so the network only has to learn the (smaller) laminar-run, separation and lift-dependent parts.

docs.title: 4. Features
docs.text:
# feature sign under reflection 1 \(m / 0.04\) − 2 \((p_e - 0.45)/0.25\) with gated position \(p_e = 0.45 + (p - 0.45)\,[1 - e^{-(m/0.01)^2}]\) + 3 \((t - 0.12)/0.06\) + 4 \((\ln\mathrm{Re} - \ln 10^6)/1.2\) + 5 \(\alpha / 10^\circ\) − 6 \(C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha)\) − 7 \(10\,C_{M,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha)\) −

The camber-position gate makes \(p\) irrelevant for symmetric sections (whose \(p\) is undefined). The gate must be an even function of \(m\): a reflected section has the same camber position. An earlier pre-release version used \(\tanh(m/0.01)\), which is odd and silently broke the symmetry for negative camber. This is why weights files carry a feature-version number (currently 2) and old files are refused. A regression test proves the reflection self-test detects that bug.

docs.title: 5. Exact reflection symmetry
docs.text:
Reflecting a section about its chord line, \(\mathcal{R}: (m, p, t, \mathrm{Re}, \alpha) \mapsto (-m, p, t, \mathrm{Re}, -\alpha)\), must give \(C_L \to -C_L\), \(C_M \to -C_M\) and the same \(C_D\). Write \(\phi(x)\) for the feature vector and \(S\) for the diagonal sign matrix of the table above. Because the panel constants of the reflected section give \(C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}(\mathcal{R}x) = -C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}(x)\) and likewise for \(C_M\), and the gate is even,

\[ \phi(\mathcal{R}x) = S\,\phi(x), \qquad S^2 = I. \]

With any network \(f = (f_L, f_D, f_M)\), the model outputs

\[ \Delta C_L = \tfrac12[f_L(\phi) - f_L(S\phi)],\quad \Delta\ln C_D = \tfrac12[f_D(\phi) + f_D(S\phi)],\quad \Delta C_M = \tfrac12[f_M(\phi) - f_M(S\phi)]. \]

At \(\mathcal{R}x\) these become \(\tfrac12[f_L(S\phi) - f_L(\phi)] = -\Delta C_L\), and similarly for the other two outputs, for every choice of weights. The baselines transform the same way (\(C_{D,0}\) depends only on Re and \(t\)). Hence

\[ C_L(\mathcal{R}x) = -C_L(x), \qquad C_D(\mathcal{R}x) = C_D(x), \qquad C_M(\mathcal{R}x) = -C_M(x) \]

holds exactly, up to floating-point round-off. In particular a symmetric section at zero incidence has exactly zero lift and moment. This is not only argued: every benchmark run executes neuralnaca.model.check_reflection, which compares predictions for 400 random signed-camber conditions with predictions for their reflections, each with its own panel solve. Property-based tests check the same thing for random networks.

Inside the shipped domain all sections have \(m \ge 0\), so the symmetry mainly acts as a hard constraint around \(m = 0\), \(\alpha = 0\) (symmetric sections must have antisymmetric polars), where it saves the network from learning it from data.

docs.title: 6. Network and ensemble
docs.text:
• Five independent multilayer perceptrons (7 → 128 → 128 → 128 → 128 → 3, SiLU), evaluated together with batched matrix products. Each member is initialised independently and draws its own minibatches.
  • Raw outputs are scaled by \((0.1, 1, 0.01)\) for \((C_L, \ln C_D, C_M)\) and added to the baseline \((C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}, \ln C_{D,0}, C_{M,\mathrm{inv}})\).
  • The prediction is the ensemble mean (for drag, the mean of \(\ln C_D\)). The member spread is reported as *_std.

docs.title: 7. Training
docs.text:
• Data: converged XFOIL runs of a scrambled Sobol design over the domain (4,096 runs for the shipped model, of which 93 % converged).
  • Loss: smooth-L1 (Huber, \(\beta = 0.1\)) on \((C_L, \ln C_D, C_M)\) weighted by \((1/0.01, 1/0.03, 1/0.002)\), roughly the inverse of the accuracy of interest. The L1 tail makes training robust to the occasional erratic XFOIL point near stall.
  • Optimiser: Adam, one-cycle schedule with peak learning rate \(3\times10^{-3}\), 18,000 steps, batch 512 per member.
  • Averaging: an exponential moving average of the weights (decay 0.9995) over the second half of training gives the final model.
  • Optional residuals (TrainConfig(residuals=True)): autograd penalties on 4,096 unlabelled collocation points. They are the pre-stall lift slope within [0.5, 1.3] × the inviscid slope, a bound on \(|d^2C_L/d\alpha^2|\), and \(d\ln C_D/d\ln\mathrm{Re} \le 0.1\). Each band holds for 97-99 % of XFOIL polar intervals. They do not improve accuracy and make training several times slower (both measured in the ablation).

Provenance of the hyper-parameters. They were chosen during development on separate XFOIL draws, never on the benchmark test sets, and frozen before the benchmark. Replications 3 and 4 were generated after the code freeze. The recipe was not changed after their results were seen.

docs.title: 8. Training support
docs.text:
neuralnaca.support.SupportModel estimates where the model has training support:

  • \(P(\text{XFOIL converges})\) is a distance-weighted vote of the 10 nearest training conditions (converged or not) in the unit-scaled input space;
  • a prediction is supported if it is in the domain, that probability is at least 0.5, and the predicted \(C_D\) does not exceed the largest converged training drag.

It is deliberately simple and transparent. Its performance on held-out data is reported in Results.

docs.title: In Python
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import neuralnaca

# one condition: scalar in, scalars out
aero = neuralnaca.get_aero("NACA 2412", alpha=4.0, Re=1e6)
print(float(aero["CL"]), float(aero["CD"]), float(aero["CM"]))

# a polar: arrays broadcast like NumPy
alpha = np.arange(-4.0, 12.1, 1.0)
polar = neuralnaca.get_aero("4412", alpha=alpha, Re=3e5)
print(polar["CL"].shape)                      # (17,)

# non-integer sections: give m, p, t directly (fractions of chord)
aero = neuralnaca.get_aero(m=0.025, p=0.45, t=0.105, alpha=2.0, Re=2e6)

Every call returns a dictionary of NumPy arrays with the broadcast shape of the inputs:

key meaning CL, CD, CM lift, drag and quarter-chord pitching-moment coefficients (ensemble mean; CD = exp(mean ln CD)) CL_std, lnCD_std, CD_std, CM_std spread of the 5 ensemble members (a heuristic error indicator, not a calibrated interval) in_domain the condition lies inside the validated domain xfoil_convergence estimated probability that XFOIL itself converges here (from the training data) supported in the domain and backed by training data; see Knowing when not to trust a prediction

Conditions outside the domain or without training support raise a DomainWarning / UnsupportedWarning (both are UserWarnings); pass on_domain_error="raise" to turn them into errors or "ignore" to silence them.

For repeated use, keep a model object (this is what get_aero does internally):

from neuralnaca import NeuralNACA

model = NeuralNACA.pretrained()
print(model)                                   # variant, ensemble size and weight fingerprint
out = model.predict("0012", alpha=[-2.0, 0.0, 2.0], Re=5e5)
pol = model.polar("6409", Re=1e6)              # alpha from -5 to 15 deg in 0.5 deg steps

docs.title: Reproducing the results
docs.text:
Every number in this documentation is produced by code in this repository from files in this repository, and can be re-derived at three levels of depth. Each level re-checks the central claim: lower MAE than NeuralFoil-xxxlarge for \(C_L\), \(\ln C_D\) and \(C_M\), with the 95 % interval excluding parity.

git clone https://github.com/KeepCoolWithCoolidge/NeuralNACA.git && cd NeuralNACA
python -m pip install -e ".[neuralfoil,plot,test]"
neuralnaca reproduce --level 0          # seconds-minutes, no XFOIL
neuralnaca reproduce --level 1          # retrain all replications, no XFOIL
neuralnaca reproduce --level 2          # regenerate the XFOIL data too (needs XFOIL)

The command exits with status 0 if everything reproduces and 1 otherwise; --json report.json saves the details and --seeds 0,3 restricts it to some replications. Levels 1 and 2 write into reproduction/ and never overwrite the shipped results.

docs.title: Level 0: verify
docs.text:
Inputs: shipped weights (benchmarks/models/) and shipped XFOIL test sets (data/xfoil/). Checks: every file matches the SHA-256 recorded in its result file. Predictions are recomputed, NeuralFoil is re-run, the metrics are compared with the shipped results (relative tolerance 10⁻⁴) and the claim is re-tested.

This isolates the evaluation: if level 0 passes, the published comparison follows from the published models and data. It also catches a different NeuralFoil version (reported, since its predictions may change between releases).

docs.title: Level 1: retrain
docs.text:
Inputs: the shipped XFOIL training sets. Does: trains every replication's model from scratch with the published recipe, then evaluates as in level 0.

  • Same platform and software versions: training is deterministic, so the retrained weights are bit-identical to the shipped ones and the metrics agree exactly. The development machine re-derived replications 0-2 bit for bit from the original research script. Training gave identical weights with 1 and 2 PyTorch threads, and the test suite checks determinism.
  • Different platform: floating-point summation order may differ (CPU, BLAS, PyTorch version), and training amplifies tiny differences. The metrics then differ by an amount bounded by the training-seed study: retraining the same data with different seeds is a worst case for "same recipe, different floating-point path". The tolerance is four standard deviations of that study's MAE (at least 3 %; 8.8 % with the shipped study, set by \(C_M\)), and the claim must still hold.

docs.title: Level 2: regenerate
docs.text:
Requires: XFOIL (see Installation). Does: re-runs XFOIL on the same designs (same Sobol and random seeds, so the same conditions), compares your labels with the shipped ones (convergence counts, agreement on commonly converged points), then retrains and evaluates.

With the documented XFOIL builds the labels agree exactly: a fresh build made with scripts/install_xfoil_python.sh reproduced the shipped results bit for bit, and scripts/build_xfoil_binary.sh rebuilt a byte-identical executable. With other XFOIL builds, differences concentrate near stall. Level 2 then uses a wider tolerance and the claim check as its pass criterion.

docs.title: What is shipped, and how it is protected
docs.text:
path content data/xfoil/ every XFOIL data set (inputs, outputs incl. non-converged runs, provenance) benchmarks/models/ every trained model of every experiment benchmarks/results/ every result (JSON) and the per-point predictions of the main runs benchmarks/MANIFEST.json SHA-256 of all of the above, plus the package weights and test fixtures docs/results/tables.md generated by neuralnaca report from benchmarks/results/ docs/assets/*.png generated by neuralnaca figures

The test suite (pytest -m benchmark) checks all of the following, so an inconsistency cannot go unnoticed:

  • every file matches the manifest;
  • every data set reproduces its declared design (to the last bit, except the Reynolds number, which is allowed a relative 10⁻¹² because 10**x is not bit-identical across operating systems);
  • no test airfoil appears in its replication's training set;
  • every result file matches its model and data hashes;
  • the claim holds in every replication and pooled;
  • the package's weights are the replication-0 model;
  • docs/results/tables.md is exactly what neuralnaca report produces;
  • the headline numbers in the README are the computed ones;
  • every ratio-with-interval quoted in any documentation page appears in the generated tables.

docs.title: Reference environment
docs.text: The published results were produced on Linux x86-64 with 2 CPU cores. The software versions are listed at the end of the generated tables and recorded in every result file. XFOIL solved about 12 cold-start runs per second on 2 cores (a replication's 7,096 runs in about 10 minutes); training one 5-member model took 5-7 minutes.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: All tables on this page are generated from the files in benchmarks/results/ (neuralnaca report), and all figures with neuralnaca figures. The protocol is described in Benchmark protocol. The ratios in the prose below are copied from those tables, and a test checks that they agree.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Lower mean error than NeuralFoil-xxxlarge for NACA sections, in every replication. Pooled over five replications and 13,933 held-out test points, the MAE ratios NeuralNACA / NeuralFoil are 0.62 [0.58, 0.65] for \(C_L\), 0.65 [0.62, 0.68] for \(\ln C_D\) and 0.60 [0.57, 0.64] for \(C_M\). The interval excludes 1 for all three outputs in each replication, including the two generated after the code freeze, and against every NeuralFoil model size.
  2. The typical error is about 2.3-3x smaller (medians), but the largest errors are not smaller. The RMSE ratios are 0.97 [0.82, 1.15] (\(C_L\)), 0.88 [0.80, 0.97] (\(\ln C_D\)) and 0.99 [0.82, 1.21] (\(C_M\)). Rare large errors in a sparsely sampled corner (high camber, low Re, negative incidence) offset the typical-case advantage for \(C_L\) and \(C_M\). See Limitations.
  3. The main reason NeuralNACA wins is geometry. NeuralFoil cannot represent a NACA section exactly; it analyses an 8+8-weight Kulfan fit of it. That fit is geometrically excellent, yet XFOIL's answer for the fitted shape differs from that for the exact section by about as much as NeuralFoil's entire error.
    • Scored against XFOIL on the fitted shape (what NeuralFoil actually analyses), NeuralFoil is more accurate than NeuralNACA is against XFOIL on the exact shape (ground-truth study below).
    • Even a plain MLP without any physics, trained on 4,096 exact-geometry XFOIL runs, beats NeuralFoil (ablation).
    • NeuralNACA is therefore the better tool for NACA 4-digit sections, because it models them exactly and specialises. It is not a better XFOIL emulator in general.
  4. The ground-truth protocol hardly matters; the geometry does. Against XFOIL run with NeuralFoil's own warm-started sweep protocol on the exact geometry, the ratios are 0.61 [0.54, 0.67], 0.67 [0.61, 0.73] and 0.62 [0.56, 0.68]. Against XFOIL on NeuralFoil's Kulfan geometry, NeuralFoil wins (e.g. 1.92 [1.73, 2.10] for \(C_L\), cold start).
  5. Of the physics ingredients, the panel-method backbone is what matters. Removing it increases the MAE by 21-41 %. Mirror symmetry and the drag prior change the MAE by at most 4 %; they guarantee consistency rather than accuracy. Autograd PINN residuals do not help and make training 4.5 times slower.
  6. Break-even with NeuralFoil is at about 2,000 XFOIL runs (0.026 % of NeuralFoil's). With 8,192 runs (one replication) the error is about half of NeuralFoil's.
  7. Variability comes from the data, not the training. Retraining on the same data with other seeds changes the MAE by about 1-2 % (standard deviation); across replications the ratio has a standard deviation of 0.03-0.06.
  8. The warning signals are informative but imperfect. The support flag catches 36-47 % of the conditions where XFOIL fails and wrongly flags under 0.5 % of converged ones. The ensemble spread has a rank correlation of 0.58-0.69 with the actual error.
  9. Speed is comparable to NeuralFoil and about 40-1,400 times faster than XFOIL, depending on the batch shape.

docs.title: Sensitivity to the definition of the XFOIL ground truth
docs.text:

docs.title: What is predicted
docs.text:
For a NACA 4-digit section with maximum camber m, camber position p and thickness t (fractions of chord), chord Reynolds number Re and angle of attack alpha (degrees), NeuralNACA predicts what XFOIL 6.99 computes with free transition (n_crit = 9, transition location free on both surfaces), Mach 0, 279 panels and a cold start:

  • CL: lift coefficient,
  • CD: drag coefficient (viscous: friction plus pressure drag),
  • CM: pitching-moment coefficient about the quarter chord, nose-up positive.

The model learns XFOIL's answers; it is not an independent CFD solver, and any error XFOIL makes (near stall, for example) is inherited. See Limitations.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
NeuralNACA.predict(airfoil=None, *, alpha, Re, m=None, p=None, t=None, on_domain_error="warn", return_members=False)
  • airfoil: a designation such as "2412", "NACA 2412", "naca2412" or "NACA-2412". Alternatively pass m, p, t (non-integer sections are fine). p is ignored when m == 0.
  • alpha, Re and m, p, t broadcast against each other with NumPy rules, so alpha can be a column vector and Re a row vector to get a 2-D table:
import numpy as np
from neuralnaca import NeuralNACA

model = NeuralNACA.pretrained()
out = model.predict("4412", alpha=np.arange(-4, 13)[:, None], Re=np.array([2e5, 1e6, 5e6]))
out["CL"].shape        # (17, 3)

docs.title: The validated domain
docs.text:
parameter range maximum camber m 0 to 0.08 (NACA first digit 0-8) camber position p 0.2 to 0.7 (second digit 2-7; irrelevant for symmetric sections) thickness t 0.06 to 0.18 (last two digits 06-18) Reynolds number 1e5 to 1e7 angle of attack -5 to 15 deg

Every reported accuracy number refers to this box. Outside it, the model extrapolates and a DomainWarning is issued. neuralnaca.DEFAULT_DOMAIN.contains(m, p, t, Re, alpha) performs the same check.

docs.title: Knowing when not to trust a prediction
docs.text:
Two independent signals are provided.

1. Training support (supported, xfoil_convergence). XFOIL does not converge everywhere inside the box; the main region is deep stall of thin sections at low Reynolds number (see the map below). The model never saw data there, and its predictions there are unconstrained extrapolations. Drag in particular can become absurd: for example C_D > 1 for NACA 0006 at Re = 1e5 and 15 degrees. Such conditions are flagged:

  • xfoil_convergence is a distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbour vote (k = 10) over the converged and non-converged runs of the training set. It costs no extra XFOIL runs.
  • supported additionally requires the predicted CD not to exceed the largest drag in the converged training data (0.156).
  • an UnsupportedWarning is raised for such conditions inside the domain.

On held-out data the flag catches 36-47 % of the conditions where XFOIL fails and wrongly flags well under 1 % of those where it converges. XFOIL's failures are partly random, so no estimate based on neighbouring conditions can catch them all. Details are in Results.

2. Ensemble spread (CL_std, lnCD_std, CM_std). The five members agree closely where data are dense and disagree where the model is uncertain. On the held-out test sets the spread's rank correlation with the actual error is 0.58-0.69, and 15-19 of the 20 largest \(C_L\) errors of each replication have a spread in the top 5 % (table in Results). The spread is a ranking signal, not a calibrated confidence interval. A practical rule: treat predictions whose CL_std is far above the typical value for nearby conditions with suspicion.

out = model.predict("8412", alpha=-4.0, Re=1.2e5)     # high camber, low Re, negative incidence: a hard corner
print(out["CL"], out["CL_std"], out["supported"])

docs.title: Gradients
docs.text: The panel method, the features and the network are all PyTorch operations, so derivatives with respect to the inputs are available through autograd. Build the inputs yourself with neuralnaca.model.to_tensors / neuralnaca.model.make_inputs and call the network directly; see the source of neuralnaca.training.physics_residuals for a worked example (it differentiates CL with respect to alpha and ln CD with respect to ln Re).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: A prediction costs one small panel solve per distinct airfoil (memoised per model instance) plus a forward pass of the 5-member ensemble. Polars and batches of conditions on the same section are therefore cheap; thousands of distinct sections cost a few milliseconds each on a CPU.

docs.title: Training your own model
docs.text: The shipped model was trained on 4,096 XFOIL runs. The same pipeline trains a model on any data set you generate, for instance with more runs, another domain or another transition criterion.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
# 1. sample a space-filling design and run XFOIL on it (needs XFOIL)
neuralnaca generate --n 8192 --kind sobol --seed 7 --out my_train.npz
neuralnaca generate --n 2000 --kind random --seed 1007 --out my_test.npz

# 2. train (5-member ensemble, 18,000 steps: ~5-7 min on 2 CPU cores)
neuralnaca train --data my_train.npz --out my_model.npz

# 3. evaluate against XFOIL (and NeuralFoil)
neuralnaca evaluate --weights my_model.npz --data my_test.npz --neuralfoil xxxlarge

# 4. use it
neuralnaca predict 2412 --re 1e6 --weights my_model.npz

train also writes my_model.support.npz (the training-support model), which NeuralNACA.load("my_model.npz") picks up automatically.

Designs

Use --kind sobol with a power of two for training sets: scrambled Sobol points fill the domain evenly, and every prefix of length 2^k is itself balanced (the data-efficiency study relies on this). Use --kind random for test sets, so that the test error is an unbiased estimate of the domain-averaged error, and use a different seed than for training.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
from neuralnaca.data import generate_dataset, pack_dataset
from neuralnaca.xfoil import detect_xfoil
from neuralnaca.training import TrainConfig, train_ensemble
from neuralnaca.model import save_model
from neuralnaca.support import SupportModel

if __name__ == "__main__":                       # required: XFOIL runs in spawned worker processes
    cfg = detect_xfoil()
    ds = generate_dataset(4096, "sobol", seed=0, cfg=cfg, path="train.npz")

    data = pack_dataset(ds)                       # converged points only (the others stay in the file)
    net = train_ensemble(data, TrainConfig(seed=0))
    save_model(net, "model.npz", {"note": "my model"})
    SupportModel.from_dataset(ds).save("model.support.npz")

docs.title: Hyper-parameters
docs.text:
TrainConfig holds the recipe; its defaults are exactly what produced every published number (a test fails if they change).

field default meaning ensemble 5 independent networks trained together steps 18000 optimiser steps (one-cycle schedule) batch_size 512 minibatch per member (each member draws its own) lr 3e-3 peak learning rate (Adam) huber_beta 0.1 smooth-L1 transition on the scaled outputs ema 0.9995 weight averaging over the second half of training width, depth 128, 4 hidden units / layers (SiLU) variant "full" "plain", "no_panel", "no_symmetry", "no_drag_prior" remove one ingredient (ablations) residuals False add the autograd physics residuals (needs collocation points)

Training is deterministic for a given seed on a given machine and PyTorch build (the test suite checks this). Other machines may differ in the last bits, which the optimiser amplifies; Reproducing the results quantifies the resulting spread.

docs.title: Changing the domain
docs.text: neuralnaca.domain.Domain describes the box. Pass a custom domain to sample_points / generate_dataset to sample it, and to NeuralNACA(..., domain=...) so that predictions are checked against it. The input features are scaled for the default box; moderate changes are fine, but large changes (for example t up to 0.30) deserve a look at neuralnaca.model.make_inputs.

docs.title: Running XFOIL
docs.text:
neuralnaca.xfoil is a robust batch driver for XFOIL. It is used to build the data sets, but it is also useful on its own.

import numpy as np
from neuralnaca.xfoil import detect_xfoil, run_xfoil

if __name__ == "__main__":
    cfg = detect_xfoil()                                     # python module if available, else an executable
    pts = np.array([[0.02, 0.4, 0.12, 1e6, a] for a in range(-4, 13)])   # [m, p, t, Re, alpha]
    res = run_xfoil(pts, cfg, workers=4)                     # (n, 3) [CL, CD, CM]; NaN rows = not converged

Use a __main__ guard

Points are solved in worker processes started with the spawn method, which re-imports your main module. Code that calls run_xfoil must be protected by if __name__ == "__main__": (Jupyter notebooks are fine). If the workers cannot start, run_xfoil raises an error that says so rather than returning all-NaN results. workers=0 runs in-process (no crash isolation).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
XfoilConfig fixes everything that influences the answer. The defaults define the ground truth of all published results.

field default notes backend "module" "module" (xfoil-python, in-process per worker) or "binary" (one process per point) executable None path of the XFOIL program (binary backend) panels 279 nodes after XFOIL's PPAR re-panelling. 279 is AeroSandbox's default, used for NeuralFoil's data n_crit 9.0 e^N transition criterion, free transition max_iter 100 viscous Newton iterations timeout 30 s per point (binary backend) protocol "cold" "cold" or "nf-sweep" (below) geometry "naca" "naca" (exact coordinates) or "kulfan" (NeuralFoil's internal fit)

docs.title: Solution protocols
docs.text:
XFOIL's viscous solution is iterative. Near stall, and in some low-Reynolds-number cases, the result can depend on where the iteration starts, so the protocol is part of the definition of the ground truth.

  • cold (default): every point starts from a fresh boundary-layer initialisation. A point's answer does not depend on which other points were run, so data sets can be generated in any order, in parallel, and extended later.
  • nf-sweep: replicates how NeuralFoil's training data were generated. AeroSandbox's XFoil.alpha(..., start_at=0) runs a sweep of 7 angles spaced 5 degrees in one XFOIL session, split at zero: positive angles upward from the smallest positive one, the others downward after a re-initialisation, each warm-started from the previous solution, with 200 iterations. For a single target angle, neuralnaca.xfoil.sweep_chain gives the angles visited before it.

The benchmark quantifies how much the choice matters.

docs.title: Geometry representations
docs.text:
• naca: the exact coordinates from neuralnaca.naca4_coordinates (100 points per side, cosine spacing), which XFOIL re-panels.
  • kulfan: the geometry NeuralFoil actually analyses. NeuralFoil normalises the coordinates and fits 8+8 Kulfan (CST) weights; the fit is evaluated at alpha + rotation_angle and Re / scale, and the moment is transferred back to the original quarter chord, exactly as neuralfoil.get_aero_from_airfoil does. Requires aerosandbox.

docs.title: Robustness
docs.text:
• Worker processes that die inside XFOIL (segmentation fault, floating-point trap) are contained. The chunk is split in halves and retried; a single point is retried alone in a private worker, and only a point that kills its own isolated worker is reported as not converged. The test suite simulates such crashes.
  • Non-converged points, exceptions and non-physical outputs (CD <= 0) are all returned as NaN rows.
  • The python module leaks a copy of the Fortran library for every new XFoil() object, so each worker keeps one instance (with a boundary-layer reset before every point) and recycles it every 400 points.

docs.title: Data sets
docs.text: neuralnaca.data.generate_dataset samples a design, runs XFOIL and stores an XfoilDataset (.npz with points, results and JSON provenance: design, XFOIL configuration and build, time, platform). A cache file is only reused if it holds exactly the requested points and XFOIL configuration; otherwise it is regenerated. See File formats.

docs.title: neuralnaca.panel
docs.text:
Differentiable Hess-Smith panel method (the "physics" backbone of the surrogate).

Inviscid, incompressible potential flow around the section is represented by a constant-strength source on every panel plus one vortex strength shared by all panels; the flow-tangency condition at the panel midpoints and the Kutta condition (equal tangential velocity magnitude on the two trailing-edge panels) close the linear system.

Because potential flow is linear in the free-stream vector, two unit solutions (free stream along x and along y) are enough to express the inviscid lift and moment analytically for any angle of attack:

.. math::

C_{L,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha) = A_L\cos\alpha + B_L\sin\alpha, \qquad
C_{M,\mathrm{inv}}(\alpha) = A_M - (B_M\cos^2\alpha + C_M\cos\alpha\sin\alpha + D_M\sin^2\alpha)

with :math:C_L from the Kutta-Joukowski theorem (:math:C_L = 2\Gamma/(V_\infty c)) and :math:C_M about the quarter chord from integration of :math:C_p = 1 - V_t^2/V_\infty^2. The six constants depend only on geometry and are computed once per airfoil by :func:airfoil_constants; :func:inviscid then evaluates them (differentiably in alpha) inside the network.

docs.title: neuralnaca.model
docs.text:
Network architecture, input features and the weights file format.

The model predicts y = [CL, ln CD, CM] as a physics base plus a learned correction:

.. math::

y = y_\mathrm{base}(\text{panel method, flat-plate drag}) + \Delta y_\theta(\text{features})

and the correction is made exactly mirror-symmetric: reflecting a section about its chord line (:math:m\to-m, :math:\alpha\to-\alpha) must give :math:C_L\to-C_L, :math:C_M\to-C_M and the same :math:C_D. With :math:x the features and :math:\bar x the features of the reflected case,

.. math::

\Delta C_L = \tfrac12[f_L(x) - f_L(\bar x)],\quad
\Delta \ln C_D = \tfrac12[f_D(x) + f_D(\bar x)],\quad
\Delta C_M = \tfrac12[f_M(x) - f_M(\bar x)].

This only holds if every feature transforms correctly under the reflection, which is why the camber-position gate is an even function of m (see :data:FEATURES_VERSION).

Ablation variants (used in the benchmark to measure what each piece of physics contributes) remove one ingredient at a time; "full" is the shipped model.

docs.title: neuralnaca.training
docs.text:
Training of the ensemble surrogate.

Recipe (all members trained simultaneously with batched matrix products, each on its own minibatch stream):

  • loss: smooth-L1 (Huber, beta = 0.1) on [CL, ln CD, CM] scaled by LOSS_W - robust to the occasional erratic XFOIL point near stall;
  • Adam with a one-cycle learning-rate schedule (peak 3e-3);
  • exponential moving average (EMA) of the weights over the second half of training - the EMA weights are the model;
  • optional autograd "PINN" residuals on unlabelled collocation points (off by default; in our experiments they do not improve accuracy, see the documentation).

docs.title: neuralnaca.support
docs.text:
Where is a prediction backed by training data?

XFOIL does not converge everywhere in the domain (deep stall of thin sections at low Reynolds number is the main region). The surrogate never saw data there, so its predictions are unconstrained extrapolations - drag in particular can grow without bound. The benchmark cannot score these points (XFOIL has no answer either), so they must be flagged instead.

:class:SupportModel estimates the probability that XFOIL converges at a condition from the training set itself (a distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbour vote over converged / non-converged training runs; no extra XFOIL runs), and also checks that the predicted drag stays inside the range of the training targets. A prediction is supported if it is inside the domain, the estimated convergence probability is at least threshold and CD does not exceed cd_max. The documentation reports how well this flag separates converged from non-converged held-out points.

docs.title: neuralnaca.xfoil
docs.text:
Running XFOIL: the "teacher" that generates training data and the ground truth for evaluation.

Two interchangeable backends are supported:

"module" The xfoil Python extension (https://github.com/daniel-de-vries/xfoil-python), in-process. About four times faster than the executable. One persistent instance per worker process (every new XFoil() object leaks a copy of the Fortran library), recycled every 400 points. "binary" An XFOIL 6.99 executable, one process per point (crash- and hang-proof). The polar save file is parsed.

Two solution protocols:

"cold" (default, used for all training and test data) Every point is solved independently from a fresh boundary-layer initialisation. The answer for a point does not depend on which other points were run. "nf-sweep" Replicates the protocol of NeuralFoil's training data (asb.XFoil.alpha with start_at=0): points are reached by an angle-of-attack sweep in sweep_step increments that starts next to 0 deg on the same side of zero and is warm-started from the previous converged point; max_iter is 200. Used only in the ground-truth sensitivity study.

and two geometry representations:

"naca" The exact NACA 4-digit coordinates (:func:neuralnaca.geometry.naca4_coordinates). "kulfan" The 8+8-weight Kulfan (CST) fit that NeuralFoil makes of those coordinates internally, including NeuralFoil's normalisation (rotation / scaling) and its moment-reference correction - i.e. the geometry NeuralFoil actually analyses. Needs aerosandbox. Used only in the ground-truth sensitivity study. "naca-normalized" Control case: the exact NACA coordinates passed through the same normalisation and frame transformation as "kulfan" but without the Kulfan fit. Separates the effect of the shape fit from that of the frame handling.

Workers that die inside XFOIL (segmentation faults, floating-point traps) are contained by :func:run_xfoil: failed chunks are split and retried, and a point that kills an isolated worker is reported as not converged.

How much does the conclusion depend on how the XFOIL ground truth is defined?

The test points of replication seed are re-solved with XFOIL under four definitions (cold start vs. NeuralFoil's warm-started sweep protocol; exact NACA geometry vs. the Kulfan fit NeuralFoil analyses). The shipped model (trained on cold/naca data) and NeuralFoil are scored against each, on the points that converged under all definitions. docs.title: reproduce(level=0, seeds=None, layout=Layout(), out=None, workers=None, rel_tol=None)

Re-derive the shipped results and compare.

Levels

0 Verify: shipped weights + shipped test data -> metrics (seconds). Must agree with the shipped results to floating-point precision (rel_tol default 1e-4). 1 Retrain: shipped training data -> new weights -> metrics (~7 min per seed on 2 CPU cores). Identical on the reference platform; elsewhere the model metrics must fall inside the band set by the training-seed variance study (rel_tol default: 4 standard deviations of the MAE, at least 3 %). 2 Regenerate: your XFOIL -> new data sets -> retrain -> metrics (~20 min per seed). Data agreement with the shipped sets is reported; the claim check (CI upper bound of the MAE ratio < 1 for all three outputs) is the pass criterion.

In every level the central claim is re-checked: NeuralNACA's MAE is lower than NeuralFoil-xxxlarge's for CL, ln CD and CM with the 95 % paired-bootstrap interval excluding 1.

Per replication: the support model is built from the training set only and evaluated on the held-out test set - AUC for predicting XFOIL non-convergence, the share of converged / non-converged test points flagged, and the MAE of both models on the supported converged points. The share of the domain volume that is unsupported is estimated by Monte Carlo (n_airfoils random sections x n_conditions random (Re, alpha) each).

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
All functionality is available through neuralnaca <command> (or python -m neuralnaca <command>). Global options: --version, -v/--verbose (debug logging), --threads N (PyTorch CPU threads). Every command has --help.

command purpose needs predict polar from the shipped (or a given) model - info version, shipped model fingerprint, domain, environment, XFOIL availability - xfoil-check does your XFOIL reproduce the benchmark's build? XFOIL generate sample a design and run XFOIL on it XFOIL train train a model (and its support model) on a data set - evaluate score a model on a test set, optionally against NeuralFoil (neuralfoil) bench run one benchmark experiment into a benchmark root data or XFOIL reproduce re-derive the shipped results (levels 0, 1, 2) see Reproducing report regenerate docs/results/tables.md from the result files - figures regenerate the documentation figures matplotlib

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
neuralnaca predict AIRFOIL --re RE [--alpha A0 A1 | --alpha A B C ...] [--step S]
                   [--weights FILE] [--compare-xfoil] [--json]

Two --alpha values give a range (with --step, default 1 degree); any other count is a list of angles. Columns: CL, CD, CM, the ensemble spread of CL and of drag (in %). Conditions outside the domain are marked.

docs.title: generate
docs.text:
neuralnaca generate --n N --out FILE [--kind sobol|random] [--seed S] [--backend auto|module|binary]
                    [--executable PATH] [--panels 279] [--protocol cold|nf-sweep] [--geometry naca|kulfan]
                    [--max-iter 100] [--workers W]

docs.title: train / evaluate
docs.text:
neuralnaca train --data FILE --out WEIGHTS [--ensemble 5] [--steps 18000] [--seed 0]
                 [--variant full|no_symmetry|no_panel|no_drag_prior|plain]
neuralnaca evaluate --weights WEIGHTS --data FILE [--neuralfoil xxxlarge[,size...]] [--out JSON]

docs.title: bench
docs.text:
neuralnaca bench {main,variance,ablation,curve,protocol,support,speed} --seeds 0-4 [--root .] [--workers W] [--retrain]
                 [--residuals] [--variants a,b,...] [--sizes 512,1024,...]
experiment what it does writes main data (if absent) → train (if absent) → evaluate vs every NeuralFoil size main_s<seed>.json, main_s<seed>_pred.npz variance retrain on the same data with training seeds 101-104 variance_s<seed>.json ablation train each model variant on the same data ablation_s<seed>.json curve train on Sobol prefixes of the training set curve_s<seed>.json protocol re-solve the test set under four ground-truth definitions protocol_s<seed>.json support evaluate the support flag and the ensemble spread support.json speed time NeuralNACA, NeuralFoil and XFOIL per condition (run on an idle machine) speed.json

The full set of experiments behind the documentation, in order:

neuralnaca bench main --seeds 0-4
neuralnaca bench protocol --seeds 0
neuralnaca bench variance --seeds 0
neuralnaca bench ablation --seeds 0-2 --variants plain,no_panel,no_symmetry,no_drag_prior,full
neuralnaca bench curve --seeds 0-2 --sizes 512,1024,2048,4096
neuralnaca bench support --seeds 0-4
neuralnaca bench ablation --seeds 0 --residuals --variants full
neuralnaca bench curve --seeds 0 --sizes 8192
neuralnaca bench speed                     # on an otherwise idle machine
neuralnaca report && neuralnaca figures

docs.title: reproduce
docs.text:
neuralnaca reproduce [--level 0|1|2] [--seeds 0-4] [--root .] [--out DIR] [--json FILE]

Exit status 0 if every replication reproduces within tolerance and the central claim holds, 1 otherwise. See Reproducing the results.

docs.title: File formats
docs.text: All files are NumPy .npz archives readable with numpy.load(path, allow_pickle=False); none contains pickled objects, so loading a file from an untrusted source cannot execute code. Metadata is stored as a JSON string.

docs.title: XFOIL data sets (data/xfoil/*.npz)
docs.text:
array shape content points (n, 5) m, p, t, Re, alpha (fractions of chord, degrees) results (n, 3) XFOIL CL, CD, CM; NaN rows where XFOIL did not converge (kept, so the design is complete) meta () str JSON: design (n, kind, seed, domain), xfoil (configuration + build), created_utc, platform

File names: {train|test}_{n}_s{seed}_{tag}.npz, where tag is p279_nc9 for the default ground truth and adds _{protocol}_{geometry}_it{max_iter} otherwise. Load with neuralnaca.data.XfoilDataset.load.

docs.title: Weights (*.npz written by save_model)
docs.text:
array content header JSON: format (neuralnaca-weights/1), features_version (2), variant, K, din, width, depth, meta W0 ... W4, b0 ... b4 layer weights (K, d_in, d_out) and biases (K, 1, d_out), float32

Files with another format or feature version are refused (IncompatibleWeightsError). NeuralNACA.fingerprint() hashes the parameters (the shipped model is 5988ce08779e0f31).

docs.title: Support model (*.support.npz)
docs.text: array content header JSON: format (neuralnaca-support/1), cd_max, k, threshold, eps points training conditions (converged and not) converged bool per training condition

docs.title: Result files (benchmarks/results/)
docs.text:
• main_s<seed>.json: data set and model records (file names, SHA-256, sizes), training configuration, reflection-check result, NeuralFoil version, the full comparison (metrics per model, MAE/RMSE ratios with bootstrap intervals, Wilcoxon p-values, win fractions, regime breakdowns) and the software environment.
  • main_s<seed>_pred.npz: per-point test conditions, XFOIL targets and the predictions of NeuralNACA and NeuralFoil-xxxlarge (for pooled analyses and figures).
  • variance_s0.json, ablation_s<seed>.json, curve_s<seed>.json, protocol_s0.json, support.json: the studies described in Results.
  • polars_reference.npz: XFOIL and NeuralFoil polars used by the figures.

benchmarks/MANIFEST.json lists the SHA-256 of every shipped data, model and result file; neuralnaca.data.verify_manifest checks them.
